situation: A brother and sister, both adults, who fell out over politics before.
topic: Abortion: they are furious, swearing at each other, bringing up old family grudges, and saying they might stop speaking.

text: Did you share that post about the Galway hospital
yeah why
Which part of it did you agree with
the part about conscientious objection being a legitimate right for doctors, it's not that controversial Róis
It's not a "legitimate right" when the result is a woman in a county with one hospital having no access. That's not a philosophical position, that's a practical outcome and people are living it.
And that account is a front. It's not some concerned GP. It's been sharing crisis pregnancy centre content for two years.
I didn't know that about the account, fair enough. still think the underlying point stands though
What underlying point. That doctors should be able to opt out of legal medical care.
that nobody should be forced to do something that goes against their conscience. you can think abortion is legal and fine and still think that
No one is forcing anyone to be an obstetrician. You choose the speciality. You don't get to then refuse the work.
We had this argument in 2018 and you said the same thing then and I let it go because I thought you'd come around. You haven't come around.
I haven't "come around" because I don't think I'm wrong
I know that's what you think.

I had a student in tears in my classroom today. Seventeen. I'm not going to tell you details but you can use your imagination. And I'm thinking about what her options actually look like right now in practice, not in theory, and then I come home and see you sharing that.
that's awful about your student. genuinely. but that doesn't mean the answer is forcing doctors to do procedures they have a moral objection to
Stop saying "moral objection" like it's neutral. Their moral objection has a physical address and it's inside someone else's body.
ok that's a bit much
Is it.
look I'm not going to change my mind tonight and neither are you. can we just
No. I'm actually asking you to think about whether you want to keep sharing this stuff publicly. Because it has an effect. It's not just an opinion.
I'm not going to be told what to share on my own phone
Right.
Do you remember what you said to me at Niamh's wedding. What you said to Mam about me in the car.
Róis that was four years ago
I know when it was.
I'm telling you that this keeps happening and I keep letting it go and I don't think I can keep doing that.
what does that mean
It means I'm serious this time. If you're going to keep publicly platforming this stuff then I don't know what we're doing here. As in, I don't know what the point of us talking is.
you're saying you'd stop talking to me over a Facebook share
I'm saying I'd stop talking to you over eight years of this. The share is just today's version.
that's not fair. I've never been anything but decent to you personally

Ciarán I love you. But decent to me personally is not the whole of it. You have a view of the world that makes my life and the lives of people I care about harder and smaller and you think it's just an opinion you're entitled to and I'm tired.
I don't know what you want me to say
I don't want you to say anything. I want you to actually think about it. Not defend it, not explain it back to me. Just think about whether it's right.
I do think about it
Okay.
look I deleted the post
I saw.
Thank you.
doesn't mean I've changed my mind fyi
I know that.
I meant what I said though. About this being a line.
yeah I know you did
mam wants to know if you're coming Sunday
Yes. What time is she saying.
she said one but you know herself
I'll go for two.

supposedly 94. inspector thinks more like 88. whole facade needs to come off

you alright

yeah same
what I said at Niamh's wedding. I know what it was
